A 1973 piece of minimalist artwork — actually, ranging for 8 stories, quite large rather than minimal — by Forrest Myers graces the blind wall of the building at 599 Broadway. It has actually been removed and rebuilt in the 2000s because of its impact on the wall it is placed on, placed higher to allow for street-level advertising below it. Because of its prominent location at the intersection of Broadway and Houston Street, it is often referred to as marking the Gateway to Soho.
Area: SoHo; Address: 599 Broadway

candidates.name: Times Square
candidates.text:
Times Square
A place filled with video screens, LED signs, and flashing lights; a world wonder or a tourist nightmare depending on your perspective, the "new" Times Square is a family-friendly theme park of themed restaurants, theaters and hotels, as well as a developing business district. The lights and signs can be viewed anytime, but the most enchanting experience comes when one visits Times Square at night, as all the signs and screens are ablaze with color. Times Square is also well known for its famous New Year's Eve ball drop. Those looking for the seedy Times Square of years past will find it around the Port Authority Bus Terminal, and on Eighth Avenue to the west.
Area: Theater District; Address: Broadway and 7th Avenue, stretching from 42nd to 48th Streets

candidates.name: Woolworth Building
candidates.text:
Woolworth Building
One of the oldest and most famous of New York's skyscrapers (dubbed the "Cathedral of Commerce"), the neo-Gothic Woolworth Building was completed in 1913 and was the world's tallest building until 1930. The building has a beautiful ornate lobby. Tours are no longer offered
Area: TriBeCa; Address: 233 Broadway

candidates.name: American Irish Historical Society
candidates.text:
American Irish Historical Society
Yet another unique but rich treat on 5th Avenue, the AIHS is a non-profit organization that educates visitors on Irish American culture and history. Immersive and traditional events are held often along with exhibits showcasing the array of unique art and music. If performing and visual arts aren't your thing, you can visit the library instead with over 10,000 books, newsletters, newspapers, and pieces of literature dating back to the 1700s that feature a wide variety of otherwise unknown topics that are great for anyone interested in European culture and history.
Area: Upper East Side; Address: 991 5th Ave; Hours: Mon-Fri 10AM-5PM

candidates.name: Ansonia
candidates.text:
Ansonia
This pretty 17-story Beaux Arts building was completed in 1904 and designed to be New York City's first air conditioned hotel. It was a residential hotel, and housed a number of very famous people, including the Hall of Fame baseball player, Babe Ruth; the Italian tenor, Enrico Caruso; the modernist composer, Igor Stravinsky; the Italian conductor of the NBC Symphony, Arturo Toscanini; and writers Theodore Dreiser and Isaac Bashevis Singer. The building is now a condominium.
Area: Upper West Side; Address: 2109 Broadway

candidates.name: Brooklyn College
candidates.text:
Brooklyn College
Brooklyn College is one of the most beautiful college campuses in the New York area. It is lovingly landscaped and includes classic buildings from the 1930s and 40s. In particular, the iconic library building with its clock tower and chimes can be seen or heard from several blocks away. The best time to visit is in April, when most of the trees are in bloom. Unfortunately, the police officers who as of September 2023 guard the entrances bar entrance to anyone without a Brooklyn College ID who shows up without permission.
Area: Bedford-Stuyvesant and Flatbush; Address: 2900 Bedford Ave; Price: Free entry if you can obtain permission in advance

candidates.name: The Coney Island Cyclone
candidates.text:
The Coney Island Cyclone
Opened in 1927, the Coney Island Cyclone or (the Cyclone) is one of the world's oldest and still operating wooden roller coasters and was declared a New York City Landmark on July 2, 1988. It was also placed on the National Register of Historic Places on June 26, 1991. Although in 1927 the roller coaster cost only 25 cents to ride, it now costs $10.
Area: Coney Island and Brighton Beach

candidates.name: Brooklyn Borough Hall
candidates.text:
Brooklyn Borough Hall
This pretty building was built as Brooklyn's city hall in 1851 and is still a very significant official building in very active use.
Area: Downtown; Address: 209 Joralemon St

candidates.name: Gowanus Canal
candidates.text:
Gowanus Canal
The anchor of the Gowanus neighborhood is this famously polluted canal. The Carroll Street Bridge is the oldest retractable bridge in the US (and one of only four left).
Area: Gowanus and Red Hook

candidates.name: Grand Army Plaza
candidates.text:
Grand Army Plaza
The gateway to Prospect Park, laid out in 1870. The Soldiers and Sailors Arch was added in 1892 as a memorial to the victorious Union Army. The Plaza itself is a large traffic circle surrounded by trees; apartment buildings; the main branch of the Brooklyn Public Library, itself a large distinctive landmark building; and a memorial bust of President John F. Kennedy. Each June, Grand Army Plaza is the focus for the Welcome Back to Brooklyn Festival for those who lived in the borough.
Area: Prospect Park

candidates.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Perpetual Help
candidates.text:
Basilica of Our Lady of Perpetual Help
If you like your churches large and impressive, OLPH is not to be missed. This Roman Catholic basilica is bigger and more ornate than Brooklyn's cathedral near downtown.
Area: Southwest Brooklyn; Address: 526 59th St

candidates.name: Bedford Avenue
candidates.text:
Bedford Avenue
The area around the Bedford Avenue subway stop is one of the most lively areas and a great place to hang out and see hipsters (as well as many tourists).
Area: Williamsburg

candidates.name: Bowne House
candidates.text:
Bowne House
The John Bowne House was built by John Bowne in 1661. It is the oldest building in Queens, and it is one of the oldest buildings in New York City. John Bowne was a Quaker who advocated religious freedom, which was later written into the Bill of Rights. John Bowne's great-grandson, Robert Bowne, strongly advocated for the end of slavery in America. The house was the home of several generations of the Bowne House until 1945, when it was donated and converted into a museum.
Area: Flushing-Northeast; Address: 37-01 Bowne Street; Price: $10 per adult, $8 per student, $8 per senior citizen

candidates.name: Louis Armstrong House Museum
candidates.text:
Louis Armstrong House Museum
A cultural highlight of the neighboring community of Corona is the Louis Armstrong House Museum, where the jazz legend lived from 1943 to his death in 1971. Armstrong and his wife Lucille chose to live in a modest single family house in an area that was once home to a number of African American performers and other luminaries. The museum preserves the furnishings and artwork pretty much just as Louis and Lucille left them, and also has a collection of Armstrong's recordings and other memorabilia. The adjacent garden — Louis' pride and joy and the only thing that distinguishes the house from its neighbors on the street — is occasionally used for concerts, notably on July 4 (Louis' stated birthday) and August 4 (determined after his death to be his actual birthday).
Area: Jackson Heights; Address: 34-56 107th Street; Hours: First tour begins at 11:30 AM, last at 3:30 PM; Price: Adults: $12, seniors (65 and older), visitors with disabilities (caregivers free of charge), active duty military, students, and children: $8, children under 5: free. Tickets must be purchased in advance; no more than four visitors per tour. Tours begin every hour on weekdays, every 30 minutes on Saturdays

candidates.name: King Manor Museum
candidates.text:
King Manor Museum
The historic home of Rufus King, a signer of the U.S. Constitution. The house exhibits the story of Jamaica Village in the early 1800s.
Area: Jamaica; Address: 150-03 Jamaica Ave; Hours: Tue-Sat Noon-4PM

candidates.name: Museum of the Moving Image
candidates.text:
Museum of the Moving Image
A museum devoted to, literally, moving images, so visitors will find exhibits on zoetropes and video games in addition to film and television. They also put on a terrific screening program, with films showing continuously throughout the day.
Area: Long Island City and Astoria; Address: 36-01 35th Ave; Hours: Tue-Thu 10:30AM-5PM, Fri 10:30AM-8PM, Sat Sun 10:30AM-7PM; Price: $20 adults, $12 seniors/college students, $10 children 3-18, free children under 3. All admission free after 2PM to 6PM every Thursday. Free admission for everyone F 4PM-8PM

candidates.name: Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge
candidates.text:
Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge
A rare bit of nature in New York. While much of the reserve has been helped along by human hands, it is still well worth visiting to see what Queens looked like before all the development. There are several walks.
Area: The Rockaways; Price: Free

candidates.name: Amundsen Circle
candidates.text:
Amundsen Circle
A small park that is not much more than a clearing and some trees. A monument to the man the park was named for, Roald Amundsen, stands in the center of it.
Area: Staten Island; Address: Amboy Road & Riedel Avenue

candidates.name: New York Pass
candidates.text:
New York Pass
Also from GoCity. Grants access to over 50 top attractions with line skipping privileges. Passes are available for 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, or 10 days. You must obtain a ticket in each attraction. You can visit as many attractions as you want in the time period. Also includes a 140-page guide book, but is much better to organize your visits in advance on the internet.
Area: New York City; Price: Prices are given as adult price/child (ages 4-12) price. 1 day: $134/$99; 2 day: $199/$159; 3 day: $274/$199; 4 day: $299/$224; 5 day: $339/$244; 7 day: $379/$259; 10 day: $469/$299

candidates.name: English Comedy Showcase
candidates.text:
English Comedy Showcase
Featuring Portuguese and international acts doing their sets in English. A great way to get a deep cultural insight into life in Lisbon through laughter. Usually free entry and donation based.
Area: Lisbon; Hours: Every Tue

candidates.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
candidates.text:
Miradouro de Santa Luzia
Good viewpoint in Alfama uphill from the cathedral along tram route. Lovely view over rooftops and river.
Area: Alfama; Address: Largo Portas do Sol; Price: Free

candidates.name: Igreja do Carmo
candidates.text:
Igreja do Carmo
The hilltop church of the former convent of Carmo is a towering memorial of the 1755 earthquake, which made the roof of the church collapse, but the Gothic arches of the nave survived. The church was preserved that way and now serves as the Museu Arqueológico in the extant parts of the building. The museum houses a hodgepodge of archaeological artifacts from around Portugal and the world including mummies from South America, tombs of Portuguese rulers, and the Stations of the Cross on 18th-century painted tiles. The assorted artifacts are not well explained, but the church is a sight to see and visitors come to relax in the grassy nave of the church, and draw or photograph the spires.
Area: Bairro Alto; Address: Largo do Carmo; Hours: Oct-May: Mon-Sat 10:00-18:00; Jun-Sep: Mon-Sat 10:00-19:00; closed Sun, 1 Jan, 1 May, 25 Dec; Price: €4 (adults), €3 (students/seniors), €3.20 (Lisbon card), free (children under 15)

candidates.name: MUDE – Museu do Design e da Moda
candidates.text:
MUDE – Museu do Design e da Moda
The collection has about 1,000 items of furniture and accessories and over 1,200 pieces of haute couture clothing.
Area: Baixa; Address: Rua Augusta 24; Hours: Temporarily closed for renovations; planned reopening 2023

candidates.name: Ajuda Botanical Gardens
candidates.text:
Ajuda Botanical Gardens
The botanical garden of Ajuda is one of the oldest gardens in Europe and is considered the first in Portugal. After the earthquake that occurred in 1755, the homeless Portuguese royal family decided to build a new royal residence at Ajuda but also gardens around it. This 10-acre garden was laid out in from 1858-1873.
Area: Belém; Address: Calçada da Ajuda; Hours: Daily 09:00-20:00 (summer), 09:00-18:00 (winter); Price: €2

candidates.name: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
candidates.text:
Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
One of the best museums in Lisbon. Created from the personal collection of the art and artifact collector Calouste Gulbenkian. The collection include Egyptian artefacts; Islamic and oriental art; paintings by masters such as Rembrandt, Manet, Monet, Renoir, and Cassat; and a large collection of objects made by the Art Nouveau jeweler René Lalique. Gulbenkian was an Armenian born in the Ottoman Empire who, through his investments in Iraqi oil, became one of the wealthiest men of his time. During a journey he fell ill and had to seek medical attention in Lisbon. He fell in love with the city and decided live out his final days there. After his death his immense collections were organized into this museum. The Gulbenkian Gardens which surround the museums and foundation building are worth a …
Area: North; Address: Avenida de Berna 45A; Hours: Wed–Mon 10:00–18:00, closed Tue; Price: 10, ages 13–30 & 65+ 5, ages 0–12 free

candidates.name: Lisbon Oceanarium
candidates.text:
Lisbon Oceanarium
One of the world's largest aquariums. Built by American architect Peter Chermayeff, it hosts thousands of marine species of the oceans, such as sea otters, penguins, and sharks. The main tank is huge, representing the Atlantic environment, with hundreds of small fishes, sharks, barracuda, snappers, and a huge sunfish. Ideal for children.
Area: Parque das Nações; Price: Adults 19, seniors 65+ 13, children 4–12 10, children 0–3 free, family (2 adults + 2 children up to age 12) 47, extra child 6

candidates.name: IndieLisboa
candidates.text:
IndieLisboa
An independent film festival. In addition to screenings there is also a large number of lectures and seminars.
Area: Lisbon; Hours: May

candidates.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
candidates.text:
Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
The highest viewpoint in Lisbon, at the top of the Graça hill, spread out in front of the small Capela de Nossa Senhora do Monte (founded in 1147, remodelled in the 20th century). To the south you look down over the Castelo de São Jorge, the Mouraria and the Baixa to the Tagus estuary; to the west, from Bairro Alto out to the Monsanto forest; to the north, down the Avenida Almirante Reis valley. It sits a little further out than the viewpoints at Santa Luzia and Portas do Sol, so it is usually quieter, and it is a fine place to watch the sunset.
Area: Alfama; Address: Largo Monte, Graça; Price: Free

candidates.name: Jardim de São Pedro de Alcântara
candidates.text:
Jardim de São Pedro de Alcântara
Excellent panorama from the lovely terrace/garden on top of Elevador da Glória and northern corner of Bairro Alto.
Area: Bairro Alto; Address: Rua S. Pedro de Alcântara; Price: Free

candidates.name: Palácio Alverca
candidates.text:
Palácio Alverca
Unassuming from the outside, the interior combines neo-Gothic, neo-Arab, neo-Renaissance, neo-Rococo, Art Nouveau, and baroque elements.
Area: Baixa; Address: Rua Portas de Santo Antão 58

candidates.name: Centro Cultural de Belém
candidates.text:
Centro Cultural de Belém
CCB is a 140000 complex of artistic and cultural venues. It has spaces for meetings and conferences, performing arts (film, opera, ballet, theatre, and music), and art exhibits (art, architecture, design, and photography).
Area: Belém; Address: Praça do Império

candidates.name: Centro de Arte Moderna
candidates.text:
Centro de Arte Moderna
A museum dedicated to art since the 1950s, focusing on Portuguese artists and including other nationalities, notably British and Armenian. Part of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation.
Area: North; Address: Rua Dr. Nicolau de Bettencourt; Hours: Daily 10:00 – 18:00, closed on Tuesdays, 10:00 – 21:00 on Saturdays

candidates.name: Pavilhão do Conhecimento - Centro Ciência Viva
candidates.text:
Pavilhão do Conhecimento - Centro Ciência Viva
Ciência Viva is an interactive science and technology museum that aims to make science accessible to all, stimulating experimentation and exploration of the physical world.
Area: Parque das Nações; Address: Largo José Mariano Gago 1; Hours: Mon–Fri 10:00–18:00, Sat Sun & holidays 10:00–19:00; Price: Adults 10, seniors 65+ 7, youths 12–17 8, children 3–11 7, children 2 & under free, family (2 adults + children under 17) 25

candidates.name: Festas dos Santos
candidates.text:
Festas dos Santos
A number of large fiestas celebrating different catholic Saints, with parades during the day and fire work shows by night. The first and largest fiesta celebrates Saint Anthony on 13 June. It is followed by the celebration of Saint John the Baptist on 23 June and Saint Peter on 28 June.
Area: Lisbon; Hours: June

candidates.name: Castelo de São Jorge
candidates.text:
Castelo de São Jorge
Humans settled on this hill as early as the 8th century BCE, and the first fortifications date from the 1st century BCE. Before the Portuguese conquest in the 1147 Siege of Lisbon, the site was successively occupied by the Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Romans, and Moors. Sights within the castle include the permanent exhibition of archaeological artefacts with an emphasis on the 11th- and 12th-century Moors, ruins of the former Royal Palace of Alcáçova, a garden with native forest species, and a camera obscura showing the city's sights. The castle offers great view over the city and the river. If you have the energy, get there by walking from downtown, going through the fantastic old neighbourhood of Alfama.
Area: Alfama; Address: Rua de Santa Cruz; Hours: Mar–Oct: daily 10:00–21:00, Nov–Feb daily 09:00–18:00; Price: 15, ages 13–25 7.5, disabled or seniors 65+ 7.50, children under 12 free; guided tour 5

candidates.name: Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga
candidates.text:
Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga
Portugal's impressive national art collection, including 14-19th century European painting, artefacts of Portuguese contact with the East and Africa and a collection of ecclesiastical treasures. Highlights include Dürer's St Jerome, Hieronymus Bosch's Temptations of St Antony, Nuno Gonçalves' Adoration of St Vincent, and 16th century Japanese paintings of Portuguese traders.
Area: Bairro Alto; Address: Rua das Janelas Verdes; Hours: Tue to Sun: 10:00-18:00; Closed Mon; Price: Normal: €6.00

candidates.name: Palácio Foz
candidates.text:
Palácio Foz
A palace constructed in the 18th and 19th centuries. Visits can be arranged in advance via email. Concerts (some of them free) are offered.
Area: Baixa; Address: Praça dos Restauradores; Hours: Mon–Fri 09:30–16:00, closed Sat Sun

candidates.name: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos
candidates.text:
Mosteiro dos Jerónimos
A , the monastery was built in the 16th century and is an outstanding example of the Portuguese late Gothic Manueline style.
Area: Belém; Address: Praça do Império; Hours: Oct-May: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:30; May-Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:30; last entry 30 min before closing; closed 1 Jan, Easter, 1 May, 13 Jun, and 25 Dec; Price: €18 (adults), €9 (seniors/students/youth card), free (children under 12); free admission to the church and on first Sun of the month. Note that tickets are sold from the neighbouring archeological museum, not at the monastery entrance

candidates.name: Parque Eduardo VII
candidates.text:
Parque Eduardo VII
Formal park with expansive views down toward the city and water from Miradouro Parque Eduardo VII. Home to the wonderful Estufa Fria greenhouse gardens.
Area: North

candidates.name: Ponte Vasco da Gama
candidates.text:
Ponte Vasco da Gama
It is the longest bridge in Europe (including viaducts), and ninth longest in the world, with a total length of 17.2, including 0.829 for the main bridge, 11.5 in viaducts, and 4.8 in dedicated access roads.
Area: Parque das Nações

candidates.name: Igreja e Mosteiro de São Vicente de Fora
candidates.text:
Igreja e Mosteiro de São Vicente de Fora
Started in 1582, this Mannerist monastery wasn't completed until 1629, following the reconstruction of a 1147 church under royal decree. The church houses the Pantheon of the House of Braganza, where many monarchs, consorts, and their offspring are entombed.
Area: Alfama

candidates.name: Museu da Marioneta
candidates.text:
Museu da Marioneta
The museum covers the history of puppetry around the world, with an emphasis on Portugal. Various types of puppets are on display.
Area: Bairro Alto; Address: Convento das Bernardas, Rua da Esperança 146; Hours: Tue–Fri 10:00–18:00, Sat Sun closed Mon; Price: Admission 5, ages 13–25 2.50, 65+ or disabled 4.30, kids under 13 free; shows 7.50, kids, seniors 65+, and students under 25 5

candidates.name: Praça do Comércio
candidates.text:
Praça do Comércio
This magnificent plaza, facing the river, is the beginning of Lisboa's downtown. It is also known as 'Terreiro do Paço', meaning 'Grounds of the Palace', relating to its function before the Great Earthquake of 1755. The upper floors of the yellow buildings surrounding the square are mainly used as government offices, while the lower floors often contains cafés and restaurants. King Josef I, who ruled during the reconstruction of Lisbon, is seen as a mounted statue in the middle of the square, while the arch facing north is a tribute to the explorer Vasco da Gama.
Area: Baixa

candidates.name: Museu Colecção Berardo
candidates.text:
Museu Colecção Berardo
The permanent collection of the museum consists of the Berardo Collection, which is made up of modern and contemporary art, with major art movements like abstract expressionism, Abstraction-Création, action painting, body Art, constructivism, cubism, De Stijl, digital art, experimental art, geometric abstraction, kinetic art, minimal art, neo-expressionism, neo-plasticism, neo-Realism, op art, photography, photorealism, pop art, realism, suprematism, surrealism. Includes artists like Piet Mondrian, Andy Warhol, Roy Lichtenstein, Pablo Picasso and Jackson Pollock, and Francis Bacon.
Area: Belém; Address: Centro Cultural de Belém; Hours: 10:00-19:00; Price: €5

candidates.name: Praça Marquês de Pombal
candidates.text:
Praça Marquês de Pombal
Essentially a large roundabout with a sizeable statue of a former Portuguese prime minister in the middle.
Area: North

candidates.name: Casino Lisboa
candidates.text:
Casino Lisboa
Among the gambling opportunities here are slot machines, poker, roulette, black jack, and baccarat. They have two restaurants, four bars, two entertainment venues, and an art gallery.
Area: Parque das Nações; Address: Alameda dos Oceanos 45

candidates.name: Lisbon Cathedral
candidates.text:
Lisbon Cathedral
Built in 1147, the cathedral has survived various earthquakes and has undergone restoration, renovation, and modification over the years. Its elements include Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles. It has been a national monument since 1910.
Area: Alfama; Address: Largo da Sé 1; Hours: Mon–Sat 10:00–18:30; Price: 5, children 7–12 2.50, children 6 & under free

candidates.name: Basílica da Estrela
candidates.text:
Basílica da Estrela
This Neoclassical and Baroque basilica, dedicated to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, was built in the late 1700s by Queen Maria I in fulfilment of a vow. The Queen is entombed in the right transept. Among the artworks is a nativity scene made up of over 500 cork and terracotta figures by Joaquim Machado de Castro.
Area: Bairro Alto; Address: Praça da Estrela

candidates.name: Praça Dom Pedro IV
candidates.text:
Praça Dom Pedro IV
One of Lisbon's principal squares. A statue of King Pedro IV stands on a column in the centre. The square, a popular meeting point for local and tourists, is known for its wavy black-and-white stone pavement.
Area: Baixa

candidates.name: Medina
candidates.text:
Medina
The Medina is the old city quarter located within the sandstone city walls that give Marrakech the nickname the Red City. As an ancient hub, it contains a maze of narrow streets and outdoor marketplaces.
Area: Marrakech

candidates.name: Djemaa El-Fna
candidates.text:
Djemaa El-Fna
The highlight of any Marrakech night. Musicians, dancers, and story tellers pack this square at the heart of the medina, filling it with a cacophony of drum beats and excited shouts. Scores of stalls sell a wide array of Moroccan fare (see the Eat section) and you will almost certainly be accosted by women wanting to give you a henna tattoo. Amateur boxing matches are sometimes held. Enjoy the various shows, but be prepared to give some dirham to watch or take photos. By day it is largely filled with snake charmers and people with monkeys, as well as some of the more common stalls.
Area: Marrakech

candidates.name: The Souks
candidates.text:
The Souks
Markets of Marrakech, just adjacent to Place Djemaa El-Fna, are where you can buy almost anything, from spices to shoes, jellabas to kaftans, and tea pots to tagines. Undoubtedly, being a foreigner means you will end up paying higher prices than a native would, but be sure to bargain nonetheless. If you happen to run out of dirham, you will also find plenty of people in the souks who will eagerly exchange your dollars or euros (though a fair rate here is less likely than at an official exchange). All that said, the sellers here are much less aggressive than, say, Egypt, so have fun!
Area: Marrakech

candidates.name: Koutoubia Mosque
candidates.text:
Koutoubia Mosque
Named after the booksellers market that used to be located here. It is said that the minaret of the Koutoubia mosque is to Marrakech as the Eiffel Tower is to Paris. The minaret is visible from Gueliz which is connected to the Medina by Avenue Mohammed V. At night, the mosque is beautifully lit. The Almohad caliph Abd al-Mu'min founded the first mosque here in 1147 and built the present one beside it in 1158; the excavated remains of the first mosque can be seen on the esplanade next to it. The minaret was completed under Caliph Yaqub al-Mansur (1184 to 1199), and has inspired other buildings such as the Giralda of Seville and the Hassan Tower of Rabat. Non-Muslims are not allowed inside.
Area: Marrakech

candidates.name: Tanneries
candidates.text:
Tanneries
Visiting the tanneries can be an interesting experience. Even if some people tell you the area is only for locals, it is possible to visit the Tanneries without paying a youngster. After finding a tannery, ask one of the workers if you can visit it and take pictures
Area: Marrakech

candidates.name: Saadian Tombs
candidates.text:
Saadian Tombs
Saadian Tombs. The tombs were built in the 16th century as the dynastic necropolis of the Saadian dynasty. The complex includes the Chamber of the Twelve Columns, the Chamber of the Mihrab, the Chamber of the Three Niches and the garden tombs. The site was rediscovered in 1917 and subsequently restored and opened to visitors. The site is relatively compact and most visitors can see the main areas in 20–30 minutes. The Chamber of the Twelve Columns cannot be entered: visitors look in from an opening at its edge, originally a window in the eastern wall, and often have to wait for a turn. The entrance passage is narrow, so arriving early can help avoid queues.
Area: Marrakech; Address: Rue de la Kasbah; Hours: generally 09:00–17:00, although visitors should check current information before travelling; Price: Foreigners: adult 100 dirham, children aged 7–13 50 dirham; Moroccan nationals and residents: adult 30 dirham, child 10 dirham

candidates.name: Moroccan Culinary Arts Museum
candidates.text:
Moroccan Culinary Arts Museum
If you are interested in food and eating culture, you will enjoy this museum. Audiovisual information about the rich culinary culture of Marocco, its ingredients, techniques and traditions. You can also touch and smell many things. They also sport a very well equipped cooking school.
Area: Marrakech; Address: Rue Riad Zitoun el Jdid

candidates.name: Majorelle Gardens
candidates.text:
Majorelle Gardens
It provides an excellent respite from the hustle and bustle of the city streets, if not crowded by tourists as it sometimes is. The park was designed by the artist Jacques Majorelle in the 1920s and 1930s. Since 1980 the garden has been owned by Yves Saint-Laurent and Pierre Bergé. It boasts a collection of plants from around the globe, including what seems like every cactus species on the planet. Get here early to avoid the crowds. Inside the gardens is also the Berber Museum, which shows a slightly bigger and more modern presentation than the Dar Si Saïd. Advance bookings must be made online, it is not possible to buy a ticket at the site.
Area: Marrakech; Address: Rue Yves Saint Laurent; Hours: Oct-Apr: 08:00-17:30, May-Sep: 08:00-18:00, Ramadan: 09:00-17:00; Price: 170 dirham, 30 dirham extra for the Berber Museum

candidates.name: Dar Si Saïd Museum
candidates.text:
Dar Si Saïd Museum
Museum set in an old palace with beautiful gardens. While somewhat run-down, it is worth seeing and houses many different artifacts from Morocco through the ages, such as wood carvings, musical instruments, and weapons. It is dedicated to the Moroccan craft industry of wood, gathering a very beautiful collection of popular art: carpets, clothing, pottery and ceramics. All these objects are regional, coming from Marrakech and all the south, especially from Tensift, High Atlas, Soussthe, Anti Atlas, Bani, and Tafilal.
Area: Marrakech; Hours: 10:00–18:00; Price: Locals: adult 10 dirham, child below 12 3 dirham; tourists: adult 30 dirham

candidates.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
candidates.text:
Ben Youssef Madrasa
One of the largest madrassas in North Africa. It is a school attached to the Ben Youssef Mosque and is home to beautiful art and architecture. The present building was completed in 1564–1565 under the Saadian sultan Abdallah al-Ghalib, on the site of an earlier Marinid madrasa. It closed as a school in 1960 and reopened to visitors in 1982. Look for the 11th-century Andalusi marble basin in the prayer hall.
Area: Marrakech; Address: Kaat Benahid; Hours: 09:00–19:00 daily (during Ramadan 09:00–16:30), closed for religious holidays; Price: Foreigners 50 dirham; Moroccans (with ID) 20 dirham; children under 12 10 dirham

candidates.name: El Bahia Palace
candidates.text:
El Bahia Palace
An ornate palace complex built in the late 19th century, with courtyards, gardens, richly decorated rooms and traditional Moroccan architectural details. The palace was begun in the 1860s by Si Moussa, grand vizier to Sultan Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, and greatly expanded in 1894–1900 by his son Ba Ahmed, Grand Vizier to Sultan Moulay Abdelaziz. The main complex covers almost 2 hectares and has about 150 rooms. The main entrance is on Rue Riad Zitoun el Jedid. The palace is relatively close to other attractions in the southern Medina and can be reached on foot from Jemaa el-Fnaa. Arriving shortly after opening can be useful for visitors who want to avoid the busiest periods.
Area: Marrakech; Hours: 09:00–17:00; Price: Foreigners: adult 100 dirham, child aged 7–13 50 dirham; Moroccan/resident: adult 30 dirham, child aged 7–13 10 dirham

candidates.name: El Badi Palace
candidates.text:
El Badi Palace
The palace complex is extensive, with ruins, courtyards, underground passages and exhibitions. The terrace offers views over the surrounding Medina and the Atlas Mountains on clear days. Allow around 45–90 minutes to explore the main areas. Visitors should check current information before travelling. (updated Aug 2026)
Area: Marrakech; Address: Ksibat Nhass; Hours: 09:00-17:00; Price: Foreigners: adult 100 dirham, child aged 7–13 50 dirham; Moroccan/resident: adult 30 dirham, child aged 7–13 10 dirham

candidates.name: The Menara gardens
candidates.text:
The Menara gardens
A mixture of orchards and olive groves surrounding the water reservoir with the central pavilion which is a popular sight on tourist postcards. Not a decorative garden, and now quite run down. The pavilion was built during the 16th-century Saadi dynasty, and renovated in 1869. It has a small cafe, but it is not open all hours. There are no toilets open when the cafe is closed.
Area: Marrakech; Hours: 09:00-17:00; Price: Free admission

candidates.name: Jewish Cemetery
candidates.text:
Jewish Cemetery
The largest Jewish cemetery in Morocco, characterized by white-washed tombs and sandy graves. The men selling tickets are full of interesting information about the cemetery but you have to ask.
Area: Marrakech; Address: Avenue Taoulat El Miara; Hours: 09:00-17:00; Price: 10 dirham

candidates.name: Slat Al Azama Synagogue
candidates.text:
Slat Al Azama Synagogue
Synagogue which is not only a place of worship with a beautiful open courtyard, but also includes interesting displays about Judaism's varied history in Morocco, including photos of Jews in the Berber Mountains.
Area: Marrakech; Hours: 09:00-19:00 (closed Sat); Price: 10 dirham

candidates.name: Musée de la Palmeraie
candidates.text:
Musée de la Palmeraie
In old agricultural buildings in the Palmeraie, made out of rammed earth. The architecture itself is interesting if you haven't seen it. It offers a small collection of contemporary art, with a room dedicated to Moroccan artists (also famous ones), the international ones are rather not top-notch. The gardens are nicely made and are good place to relax in quiet.
Area: Marrakech; Address: Dar Tounsi, Route de Fès; Hours: 09:00-18:00?; Price: 40 dirham

candidates.name: Musee Farid Belkahia
candidates.text:
Musee Farid Belkahia
A museum dedicated to the renowned contemporary artist Farid Belkahia, showcasing different periods of his work
Area: Marrakech; Address: Dar Tounsi, Route de Fès; Hours: Mon-Sat

candidates.name: Maison de la Photographie
candidates.text:
Maison de la Photographie
A little photography museum, it has one of the highest roof terraces in the Medina. Ticket is also valid for Museum of Mouassin Music.
Area: Marrakech; Address: 46, Rue souk Ahal Fès; Price: 80 dirham

candidates.name: Ali Ben Youssef Mosque
candidates.text:
Ali Ben Youssef Mosque
The first mosque in Marrakesh was erected at this place by the Almoravid emir Yusuf ibn Tashfin in the 1070s. However, it was almost completely rebuilt in early 19th century by the Alaouite sultan Suleiman, with hardly any trace left of its original Almoravid or Almohad design. Non-Muslims are not allowed to enter it.
Area: Marrakech

candidates.name: Agdal Gardens
candidates.text:
Agdal Gardens
It consists of groves of orange, lemon, fig, apricot and pomegranate trees in rectangular plots, linked by olive-lined walkways. Together with the medina of Marrakech and the Menara Gardens, the Agdal Gardens were listed by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site in 1985.
Area: Marrakech; Price: 70 dirham for foreign adults

candidates.name: Almoravid Koubba
candidates.text:
Almoravid Koubba
A very small but intricate domed pavilion, known for being the only surviving example of Almoravid religious architecture (early 12th century) in Marrakech. Located across the street from the Ben Youssef Mosque, it is believed to have been an annex of the former Almoravid mosque. It was excavated in the 20th century after being half-buried for centuries. The pavilion's exterior can be easily seen from the street, so paying for entry just lets you see its interior.
Area: Marrakech; Price: 50 dirham

candidates.name: Chez Ali Fantasia
candidates.text:
Chez Ali Fantasia
Horse show, acrobats on Arabian horses firing rifles in the air, horseback acrobatics, belly dancing, etc. It takes place at night in a huge imitation of an old castle.
Area: Marrakech; Address: La Palmeraie de Marrakech; Price: €15

candidates.name: Stade de Marrakesh
candidates.text:
Stade de Marrakesh
This is multi-use but mostly for football, with a capacity of 41,356. It's the home ground of Kawkab, who play in Botola 2 the second tier. In 2025 / 26 it hosted matches in the Africa Cup of Nations.
Area: Marrakech

candidates.name: Marrakech Paragliding
candidates.text:
Marrakech Paragliding
Leave the city behind and discover the incredible beauty of Morocco from above! Enjoy an exciting tandem paragliding experience near Marrakech, surrounded by the spectacular Atlas Mountains.
Area: Marrakech; Address: Aguergour , Ouzguita 45 Km from Marrakech

candidates.name: Moratra Medina walking tour
candidates.text:
Moratra Medina walking tour
A 2- to 4-hour walk through the old city with a licensed local guide, covering how the souks and their crafts are organised and landmarks such as the Bahia Palace, Ben Youssef Madrasa and the Saadian Tombs.
Area: Marrakech; Hours: Morning or late afternoon, year-round; Price: US$20 per person in a small group, US$60 per person private

candidates.name: Les Bains de Marrakech
candidates.text:
Les Bains de Marrakech
Tourists-oriented in good sense: couples can have hammam together in a private room. Extensive list of massages and spa treatments from 30 min to a full day. Reception and attendants are proficient in speaking English, however, the scrubbing and massage personnel speak only very basic vocabulary. You need to book two days in advance.
Area: Marrakech; Address: 2 Derb Sedra, Bab Agnaou (same building as Riad Mehdi); Hours: 09:00-19:30; Price: 170–1,400 dirham

candidates.name: Thai marrakech
candidates.text:
Thai marrakech
Bann Thai institute is a beauty center based in the heart of Marrakech. His team is a graduate of the famous school of Wat Po in Bangkok. The center offers several Thai massage relaxation with a traditional Moroccan hammam natural products
Area: Marrakech; Address: Résidence Les Jasmins Apt N° 13 4ème étage Angle Av. Mohamed v et Rue Oum Errabia Guéliz

candidates.name: Banco do Brasil Cultural Centre
candidates.text:
Banco do Brasil Cultural Centre
A cultural centre with gallery, movie theatre, video room, library and stages; usually hosts the main exhibitions in town. An interesting building completed in 1906 with old-fashioned elevators/lifts.
Area: Centro; Address: Rua 1º Março 66 - Centro

candidates.name: Maracanã Stadium
candidates.text:
Maracanã Stadium
Once the world's highest capacity football venue, it was able to hold nearly 200,000 people. In modern times, the capacity has been reduced because of safety considerations, and the introduction of seating for all fans. It is undergoing renovation, to expand it to hold 80,000. The matches of Rio's football clubs like Flamengo or Fluminense are usually far from full, so go along and watch a game. There is also a Soccer Museum inside.
Area: Zona Norte; Address: Av. Presidente Castelo Branco at Av. Maracanã

candidates.name: Barra Woods
candidates.text:
Barra Woods
This 560,000-m² park is one of the most visited green areas in the Zona Oeste, with a lake, walking trails through the woods, large lawns, playgrounds, and sporting facilities.
Area: Zona Oeste; Address: Av. das Americas, km.6 - Barra da Tijuca

candidates.name: Sugar Loaf Mountain
candidates.text:
Sugar Loaf Mountain
One of the defining landmarks of the city. The cable cars take you up from for a breathtaking view of much of Zona Sul and the center, and also the city of Niteroi, just across Guanabara Bay. You have to queue again at Urca Hill (Morro da Urca) station for the second part of the ride. You can also walk up a trail to this point (start on Trilha do Morro da Urca along the shore, then climb the stairs on your left) and take the cable cars to Pão de Açucar and back to Praia Vermelha for R$92, or just back to Morro da Urca for R$59, or just down to Praia Vermelha for R$39 (full prices). This ticket office closes at 19:30, the downward trip is free after that. At Morro da Urca you can take a sightseeing helicopter trip, if you can afford it. The area is pretty secure, thanks to the various …
Area: Zona Sul; Address: Av. Pasteur 520, Urca; Hours: 08:00-21:00; Price: R$99 (online), R$110 (box office)

candidates.name: National Library
candidates.text:
National Library
The National Library offers guided tours on weekdays, showing visitors its rare collection, various bookstacks and the catalogue system. Registration with identification is required, and tours run for about an hour. They leave at 13:00 for English tours, and 11:00, 13:00 and 15:00 for Portuguese tours.
Area: Centro; Address: Av Rio Branco 219; Price: R$2 for tour

candidates.name: Tijuca National Park
candidates.text:
Tijuca National Park
A few km north of the beach, this mountainous subtropical forest is Brazil's smallest national park. It is largely hand-planted as much of the original forest was destroyed to make way for coffee plantations. Despite this it contains hundreds of species, many of which are threatened with extinction. Corcovado is to the east of the park but if you really want to appreciate what the park has to offer you have to drive along some windy, hilly roads and get out and hike. This sector of the park can be reached via Rua Boa Vista, and from São Conrado in Zona Oeste.
Area: Zona Norte; Address: Estrada da Cascatinha, 850 - Alto da Boa Vista

candidates.name: Chico Mendes Ecological Park
candidates.text:
Chico Mendes Ecological Park
This 43-hectare park has walking trails through a preserved section of the Mata Atlântica (Atlantic Forest). They also offer a guided tour of the habitats of several local endangered species, including the three-toed sloth, the broad-snouted caiman, and the red-footed tortoise. There is an exhibit hall with exhibits on local wildlife.
Area: Zona Oeste; Address: Avenida Jarbas de Carvalho 679 - Recreio dos Bandeirantes; Hours: Tue-Sun 08:00-17:00; Price: Free

candidates.name: Christ the Redeemer Statue (Corcovado peak)
candidates.text:
Christ the Redeemer Statue (Corcovado peak)
The 710 granite peak of Corcovado, capped by the famous 38-m statue of Jesus known as Christ the Redeemer (Cristo Redentor), has been the vantage point for countless picture postcards and travel posters through the ages. Its peak provides a sweeping panorama, from the interior of Guanabara Bay to the north, to Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas (Rodrigo de Freitas' Lagoon) to the south. Access to the mountain as a whole is free, but most of the good views are within the paid area of the Christ statue. You can't enter the statue itself except for a small chapel at the bottom of it.
Area: Zona Sul; Hours: 08:00-19:00; Price: R$58 adults, R$32 children/students/seniors (included in price of some transportation)

candidates.name: Passeio Público
candidates.text:
Passeio Público
Commissioned in 1779, this was to become the first public park in the Americas. Check out the original Rococo-style gate and the ironwork fountains.
Area: Centro; Address: Rua Texeira de Freitas at Rua Mestre Valentim

candidates.name: Engenhão Stadium
candidates.text:
Engenhão Stadium
Estádio Olímpico João Havelange, known by its nickname of Engenhão, is a new soccer stadium built for the Pan-American Games of 2007. A modern construction, not as big as Maracanã but still worth a visit for soccer fans. The Botafogo team plays its matches there.
Area: Zona Norte; Address: Rua Arquias Cordeiro - Engenho de Dentro

candidates.name: Pedra Branca State Park
candidates.text:
Pedra Branca State Park
The largest ecological park in the city, and the largest urban forest in the world, with 12,500 hectares. Vegetation is typical of the old Atlantic forest, and fauna includes ocelots, sloths, armadillos, and toucans. Beyond the nature, there are also ruins of several structures, such as old farmhouses.
Area: Zona Oeste

candidates.name: Arpoador
candidates.text:
Arpoador
The rocks at the Copacabana end of Ipanema beach. From here you can see a panorama including Corcovado and Sugar Loaf. It is supposed to be the best place to watch the sunset from in Rio. Reputedly a bit dangerous so go there at weekends when there are lots of people and a few police around.
Area: Zona Sul

candidates.name: Petrobras Headquarters
candidates.text:
Petrobras Headquarters
The headquarters for the federal gas (petrol) company is an interesting piece of brutalist architecture which somehow resembles a Rubik's Cube with some blocks missing.
Area: Centro; Address: Avenida República do Chile 1202

candidates.name: Grajaú State Park
candidates.text:
Grajaú State Park
This 55-hectare park preserves some of the original forest and serves as a refuge for a wide range of species including marmosets, bush dogs, guinea pigs, parakeets, vultures, and hawks. The park includes the Pedra do Andaraí, symbol of the area.
Area: Zona Norte; Address: Rua Comendador Martinelli 742 - Grajaú

candidates.name: Sítio Roberto Burle Marx
candidates.text:
Sítio Roberto Burle Marx
The garden of landscape architect and artist Roberto Burle Marx (1909-1994), with a collection of plants from all over Brazil. In 2021 it was listed as a world heritage site.
Area: Zona Oeste

candidates.name: Guanabara Palace
candidates.text:
Guanabara Palace
Former palace of the Imperial Princess, now the governor's office. Eclectic architecture. Not open to the public.
Area: Zona Sul; Address: Rua Pinheiro Machado - Laranjeiras

candidates.name: Sambódromo
candidates.text:
Sambódromo
Site of the famous Carnaval parades, the Sambódromo is a long street flanked by grandstands and VIP boxes. From the start of the year until Carnaval week, technical rehearsals (Ensaios Técnicos) free to the public are held on Saturday and Sunday evenings, with 2-3 teams performing per session.
Area: Centro; Address: Rua Marquês de Sapucaí - Praça Onze

candidates.name: Musical sidewalks of Vila Isabel
candidates.text:
Musical sidewalks of Vila Isabel
The mosaic sidewalks along Boulevard 28 de Setembro between Praça Maracanã and Praça Barão de Drummond are musical staves. Written in the stones are 20 complete musical works, including tunes by Ary Barroso, Martinho da Vila, Almirante, Noel Rosa, and other famous Brazilian composers who frequented Vila Isabel back in its Bohemian heyday. If you know who these guys are, you might also be interested in checking out the famous sculpture of Noel Rosa on this street at the entrance to the bairro.
Area: Zona Norte; Address: Vila Isabel

candidates.name: Pedra do Telégrafo
candidates.text:
Pedra do Telégrafo
Hike up this 354-m-high mountain and enjoy a beautiful view. Famous for the "cliffhanger images", which can be taken on top.
Area: Zona Oeste

candidates.name: Museum of Folklore Edison Carrero
candidates.text:
Museum of Folklore Edison Carrero
Part of the National Centre for Folklore and Popular Culture (CNFCP). The museum was created in 1968 and today has around 13,000 objects by various authors, techniques and origins, kept in technical archives, available for consultation by institution-related post-graduate specialists, by appointment.
Area: Zona Sul; Address: Rua do Catete 179

candidates.name: Selarón Steps
candidates.text:
Selarón Steps
A stairway covered by colorful tiles and the ever-evolving art work of Chilean artist Jorge Selarón.
Area: Centro; Address: Santa Teresa

candidates.name: Rio de Janeiro Zoo
candidates.text:
Rio de Janeiro Zoo
If you won't be making it to the Amazon or the Pantanal, this is a good place to see some of Brazil's more exotic creatures.
Area: Zona Norte; Address: Parque Quinta da Boa Vista - São Cristóvão

candidates.name: Indian Museum
candidates.text:
Indian Museum
Focusing on the history of Native Brazilians, with many artifacts including a home of the Umé culture. The gift shop has authentic handicrafts.
Area: Zona Sul; Address: Rua das Palmeiras 55 - Botafogo; Hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-17:30, Sat Sun 13:00-17:00

candidates.name: Valongo Wharf Archaeological Site
candidates.text:
Valongo Wharf Archaeological Site
The place where, during the first decades of the 19th century, ships carrying a total of almost a million African slaves landed. When slave trade was banned, freed slaves lived there for some time, eventually the whole area was entirely rebuilt and its dark history was forgotten until 2011, when African amulets and other items of worship were found during construction works. Nowadays the former wharf is an archaeological site and since 2017 a world heritage site.
Area: Centro

candidates.name: Train Museum
candidates.text:
Train Museum
A modest collection of 19th-century engines, train cars used by emperors and presidents, and streetcars.
Area: Zona Norte; Address: Rua Arquias Cordeiro 1046 - Engenho de Dentro; Hours: Tue-Fri 10:00-12:00 and 13:30-16.00; Sat 13:00-17:00

candidates.name: Carmen Miranda Museum
candidates.text:
Carmen Miranda Museum
Here you'll find an amusing collection of photographs, posters, musical recordings, and, of course, gigantic fruity hats worn by the singing star. The building looks like an abandoned space capsule in the middle of the park.
Area: Zona Sul; Address: Av. Rui Barbosa

candidates.name: Campo de Santana
candidates.text:
Campo de Santana
It is near the site where Brazil was declared a Republic in 1889. It's also the site of the monument for Republican leader Benjamin Constant.
Area: Centro

candidates.name: Museu do Açude
candidates.text:
Museu do Açude
The former residence of one of the founders of the Modern Art Museum, this museum hosts a collection of items from the history of Portuguese rule, including furniture, kitchenware, and an array of azulejos, or Portuguese blue tiles. There are also separate collections of Oriental art and Brazilian pop art.
Area: Zona Norte; Address: Estrada do Açude, 764 - Alto da Boa Vista; Hours: Thu-Sun 11:00-17:00

candidates.name: Museum of the Republic
candidates.text:
Museum of the Republic
The former presidential palace (1893-1960) hosts a museum of recent history and nice gardens, with an adjacent art gallery and small theatre that occasionally shows free movies. One of main features is the room where president Getúlio Vargas shot himself in 1954.
Area: Zona Sul; Address: Rua do Catete, 153 - Catete

candidates.name: Gloria Church
candidates.text:
Gloria Church
Small but interesting church built in 1739. It is more correctly known as the Outeira da Gloria, outeira in Portuguese meaning “knoll” or small hill. The church was well sited to be seen by arriving sailors sailing into Guanabara Bay. The layout consists of two intertwined octagonal prisms. There are some interesting wooden engravings and tiles from Portugal. Best accessed by one of the world’s shortest funiculars from Rua do Russel. The ride is free. Nice views.
Area: Centro; Address: Glória

candidates.name: InterContinental ANA Tokyo
candidates.text:
InterContinental ANA Tokyo
An international hotel and all staff can speak English. The rooms are a decent size compared to most American hotels. There is also a limousine bus connecting the ANA Hotel to Narita Airport - it takes approximately two hours and is available to both guests of the hotel and people with other accommodation.
Area: Akasaka; Address: 1-12-33 Akasaka

candidates.name: First Cabin Akihabara
candidates.text:
First Cabin Akihabara
Nice capsule hotel that's more spacious than your usual affair. Unlike other capsule hotels, the capsules are not vertically stacked, and the first class cabins have enough room to stand in and lay out your luggage. The staff speaks English well enough to check you in and respond to any special requests. Breakfast costs ¥300 and includes two rice balls (onigiri) and miso soup, and there are also vending machines in the lobby for drinks and hot meals.
Area: Akihabara; Address: 3-38 Sakuma, Chiyoda-ku; Price: Singles ¥4800-5800

candidates.name: Khaosan Tokyo Guesthouse
candidates.text:
Khaosan Tokyo Guesthouse
This group of guest houses has 3 hostels within 5 minutes of Asakusa station. They also run a travelers' bar and you get 1 free drink when you stay. There are dormitories as well as private rooms available.
Area: Asakusa; Price: ¥2000

candidates.name: Hotel Kizankan
candidates.text:
Hotel Kizankan
This basic business hotel is convenient for those visiting Tokyo University. Minutes from the Hongo-Sanchome stations of the Oedo and Marunouchi subway lines, and close to the many small restaurants in front of the university. Little English is spoken, but foreigners are welcome.
Area: Bunkyo; Address: 4-37-20 Hongo; Price: Singles from ¥7980, twins from ¥8925

candidates.name: Tokyo Central Youth Hostel
candidates.text:
Tokyo Central Youth Hostel
Located on the 18th and 19th floors of a high-rise, with great views over the city (including a hot tub and baths overlooking the lights and skyscrapers of Shinjuku) and comfortable rooms. Formerly known as Tokyo International Hostel.
Area: Chiyoda; Address: 1-1 Kagurakashi, Shinjuku-ku; Price: ¥4050

candidates.name: Tokyu Stay Nihombashi
candidates.text:
Tokyu Stay Nihombashi
Slight discounts are offered for extended stays. Part of the Tokyu Stay chain, these hotels are popular with business travelers. The small kitchenettes, washer/dryers, and free LAN access in all rooms makes these a good value.
Area: Chuo; Address: 4-7-9 Nihombashi-Honcho; Price: Singles start at ¥9,450, twin rooms ¥17,850

candidates.name: Smile Hotel Tokyo Ayase-ekimae
candidates.text:
Smile Hotel Tokyo Ayase-ekimae
Convenient to visit East Tokyo. Near Ayase station in Adachi-Ku. It is on the Chiyoda line which means easy access to central Tokyo, it takes about 30-40 minutes to Shibuya, Shinjuku and Ikebukuro.
Area: East

candidates.name: Hotel Excellent Ebisu
candidates.text:
Hotel Excellent Ebisu
Affordable and clean business hotel, with a total of 127 rooms (single, double, and twin). Breakfast is available at an additional charge.
Area: Ebisu; Price: Single ¥9,950, Double ¥12,700, Twin ¥14,600, add ¥100 if single occupancy in a double or a twin room

candidates.name: Hotel Monterey Ginza
candidates.text:
Hotel Monterey Ginza
This hotel, owned by a Japanese businesswoman, caters to women. Located in the heart of the Ginza district, the Monterey offers comfortable rooms and has a friendly front desk staff. Across the street is one of the many AM/PM convenience stores where a traveler may purchase needed items 24 hr a day.
Area: Ginza; Address: 2-10-2 Ginza

candidates.name: Tokyu Stay Gotanda
candidates.text:
Tokyu Stay Gotanda
This chain of hotels is very popular with business travelers. When the Shibuya or other branches are full (as is often the case) this is a good alternative. All rooms have a clothes washer/drier and most have a kitchenette so this is a good option for longer stays.
Area: Gotanda; Address: Shinagawa-ku, Higashi Gotanda 1-12-2; Price: Single ¥9,400-11,000

candidates.name: Westin Hotel Tokyo
candidates.text:
Westin Hotel Tokyo
Renovated in 2023. Rooms are elegant and well furnished with over-sized bathrooms and workout areas. Their in house spa offers a variety of services.
Area: Meguro; Address: 1-4-1 Mita; Price: ¥33,000 and up

candidates.name: Sheraton Miyako Hotel Tokyo
candidates.text:
Sheraton Miyako Hotel Tokyo
Reasonably swish hotel. Good for a layover with its back garden and downstairs cigar bar. Probably a poor option for a tourist unless you have business in the area as it's about a ten minute walk from nearby transport and not close to attractions.
Area: Minato; Address: 1-1-50, Shirokanedai

candidates.name: Tokyo Bay Ariake Washington Hotel
candidates.text:
Tokyo Bay Ariake Washington Hotel
The third hotel in the area (just north of the Tokyo Big Sight exhibition center). Targeting business travelers it is the cheapest hotel in the area.
Area: Odaiba; Address: 3-1-28 Ariake, Koto-ku; Price: Rates ranging from ¥9,950 (single) to ¥18,000 (twin)

candidates.name: 328 Hostel & Lounge
candidates.text:
328 Hostel & Lounge
This hostel contains dormitory rooms with bunk beds. Single travelers share a room with other people of the same gender, while two travelers can use a private dorm room. From Haneda Airport, take a Keikyu train marked as a Local (普通) or Express (急行) to Anamori-Inari Station and walk south for about 500 meters.
Area: Ota; Address: 3-2-8, Haneda; Price: ¥3,280 single, ¥7,600 double

candidates.name: the b
candidates.text:
the b
Super centrally located at Roppongi Crossing (center of night life area), 2 minutes to subway Hibiya and Oedo line, renovated in spring 2006, nice but small rooms.
Area: Roppongi; Address: 3-9-8 Roppongi; Price: From ¥9000, with regular special discount offers when booking via the homepage (special offers available in Japanese only)

candidates.name: Mustard Hotel
candidates.text:
Mustard Hotel
Modern hotel with different room types, all of which have a record player and records that can be borrowed free of charge. The reception area features Sidewalk Coffee Roasters, serving coffee and bagels.
Area: Setagaya; Address: 3-9-19 Kitazawa

candidates.name: Cerulean Tower Tokyu Hotel
candidates.text:
Cerulean Tower Tokyu Hotel
A popular high-end hotel near the station. Also contains a large office complex, as well as some very expensive restaurants. It provides free Wi-Fi, and you can use fitness and swimming pools for free when you stay.
Area: Shibuya; Address: 26-1 Sakuragaoka-cho; Price: ¥33,000

candidates.name: Toyoko Inn Shinagawa Aomono-yokocho-eki
candidates.text:
Toyoko Inn Shinagawa Aomono-yokocho-eki
An alternative Toyoko Inn, five minutes south of Shinagawa by Keikyu local train. Availability is generally better here than the other Toyoko Inn, and the hotel is directly connected to the Keikyu line.
Area: Shinagawa; Price: Rack rates from ¥6,720

candidates.name: Tokyu Stay Shinbashi
candidates.text:
Tokyu Stay Shinbashi
Part of the Tokyu Stay chain, these hotels are popular with business travelers. The small kitchenettes, washer/dryers, and free LAN access in all rooms makes these good value.
Area: Shinbashi; Address: 4-23-1 Shinbashi; Price: Singles start at ¥9,450, doubles at ¥17,850 per night. Slight discounts are offered for extended stays

candidates.name: Sakura Hotel Hatagaya
candidates.text:
Sakura Hotel Hatagaya
Affordable hotel with a round-the-clock cafe offering a variety of Asian ethnic dishes. Staff can speak English.
Area: Shinjuku; Address: 32-3 Hatagaya Shibuya-ku; Price: Single rooms ¥6930, double rooms ¥9000, twin & triple room with breakfast

candidates.name: Park Hotel Tokyo
candidates.text:
Park Hotel Tokyo
If the Park were any more minimalist, it wouldn't be here at all. This sky-high establishment boasts a light and airy foyer, with inviting lounge and restaurant adjoining.
Area: Shiodome; Address: Shiodome Media Tower, 1-7-1, Higashi Shimbashi; Price: Rooms start from ¥19,500 single

candidates.name: The Koenji
candidates.text:
The Koenji
The place has 7 rooms (4 single and 3 double) all efficiently laid out. There may be noise from nearby bars on weekends.
Area: Suginami; Address: 2F,3F 3-22-2 Koenji; Price: ¥2500

candidates.name: Juyoh Hotel
candidates.text:
Juyoh Hotel
Very nice cheap hotel, prices ranging from ¥3200 for a single (¥2980 with a discount coupon printable from their web page, includes cleaning service every other day) to ¥6400 for a double (¥5960 with coupon). Internet access available in the lobby, five PC's and Macs available; wireless and ethernet support for laptops.
Area: Taito; Address: 2-15-3 Kiyokawa

candidates.name: Kimi Ryokan
candidates.text:
Kimi Ryokan
This friendly if very tourist-oriented minshuku (no, it's not a ryokan) is an excellent option for first time travelers to Tokyo. It is reasonably priced (¥4500) and has English speaking staff. A nice way to spend your first night on a tatami.
Area: Toshima; Address: 2-36-8 Ikebukuro

candidates.name: Sutton Place Hotel
candidates.text:
Sutton Place Hotel
Mid-range hotel, in the R-Hotels Group. Rooms have en-suite toilet. Staff speaks English. Breakfast included. Free internet access in the lobby. The hotel is in a quiet street in Ueno, 2 minutes walking from JR Ueno Station and 5 minutes walking from subway Ueno Station. From Keisei Ueno, terminating station of the Skyliner from Narita Airport, the walk is about 10 minutes.
Area: Ueno; Address: 7-8-23, Ueno, Taito-ku; Price: ¥7000

candidates.name: Hotel Asia Center of Japan
candidates.text:
Hotel Asia Center of Japan
Excellent budget hotel – no amenities like a gym or spa, but friendly staff, small but well-appointed rooms, restaurant. Free high-speed internet in room, coin internet in lobby. Laundry available.
Area: Akasaka; Address: Akasaka 8-10-32; Price: ¥8000

candidates.name: Remm Akihabara Hotel
candidates.text:
Remm Akihabara Hotel
Small rooms that are priced in a mid-range of hotel rates. Despite the small rooms, the hotel is very comfortable and rooms are well appointed.
Area: Akihabara; Address: 1-6-5 Sakuma, Chiyoda-ku; Price: Singles from¥14,275, twins ¥24,450

candidates.name: Sakura Hostel Asakusa
candidates.text:
Sakura Hostel Asakusa
The largest hostel in Tokyo, behind a theme park and with a direct view of Tokyo Skytree, the world's second tallest structure. Accommodations for individual backpackers, families, and group travelers. Very friendly English speaking staff.
Area: Asakusa; Address: 2-24-2 Asakusa; Price: From ¥2940 person/night

candidates.name: Toyoko Inn Korakuen Bunkyokuyakusho-mae
candidates.text:
Toyoko Inn Korakuen Bunkyokuyakusho-mae
Toyoko Inns are inexpensive business hotels, but have a good range of amenities. Their access maps are exceptionally clear, with an English version for you and Japanese for the taxi driver. This one is not near any tourist destinations but convenient to major subway lines.
Area: Bunkyo; Price: Singles, doubles and twins, all under ¥10,000

candidates.name: Imperial Hotel Tokyo
candidates.text:
Imperial Hotel Tokyo
Never mind upstarts like the Park Hyatt, this is the grand old dame of Tokyo's hotels with over 115 years of history behind it and legendary service fit for an Emperor. Standard rooms are musty, but the refurbished Imperial Floor rooms are nice. The hotel overlooks Hibiya Park and is only a short walk from the Imperial Palace and the Ginza.
Area: Chiyoda; Address: Uchisaiwaicho 1-1-1; Price: ¥43,000 and higher

candidates.name: Chelsea International Hostel
candidates.text:
Chelsea International Hostel
Small and clean. Internet access, 24-hour reception. All guests must show a passport when checking in, including U.S. citizens.
Area: Chelsea; Address: 251 West 20th St

candidates.name: The Bowery Grand Hotel
candidates.text:
The Bowery Grand Hotel
Rock bottom accommodation. Single rooms are smaller than the size of a double bed, and the place is not exactly sparkling. Rooms have no roof, so there is no privacy, and you can hear everyone else packed in inches away from you. Wifi is slow. But you can't beat the price.
Area: Chinatown; Address: 143 Bowery, New York; Price: $50

candidates.name: The Bowery Hotel
candidates.text:
The Bowery Hotel
Fabulously dark and moody, this newish old-school hotel is cool and charming in a low-key way. Rooms are spacious with plenty of light and dark hardwood floors, and the more expensive ones come with fantastic bathtubs. The bar and lobby are popular hangouts.
Area: East Village; Address: 335 Bowery; Price: From $350

candidates.name: Andaz Wall Street, A Hyatt Hotel
candidates.text:
Andaz Wall Street, A Hyatt Hotel
The only hotel on Wall Street featuring 253 rooms that begin at a very large 345 sq ft (32 m²). All rooms come with free internet, free minibar (except alcohol), free gym access, and free light refreshments in the lobby.
Area: Financial District; Address: 75 Wall St; Price: $250-350

candidates.name: The MAve Hotel
candidates.text:
The MAve Hotel
Comfortable, stylish place. This space was built in 1902 but still feels modern with vibrant murals on the walls and sleek bamboo floors. Offers a complimentary breakfast. Occasionally, Groupon has deals for this hotel.
Area: Gramercy Flatiron; Address: 62 Madison Avenue; Price: $170 and up depending on the season

candidates.name: Washington Square Hotel
candidates.text:
Washington Square Hotel
This hotel offers art deco styled furnishings and complimentary internet access at the lobby bar and considers itself a haven for writers, artists and visitors.
Area: Greenwich Village; Address: 103 Waverly Pl

candidates.name: Holiday Inn Lower East Side
candidates.text:
Holiday Inn Lower East Side
A fairly standard Holiday Inn except for the Retro diner serving as the hotel's restaurant. This is the hotel located the deepest into the Lower East side of all, and hence it is in a slightly deserted area, facing a parking crater.
Area: Lower East Side; Address: 150 Delancey Street

candidates.name: Soldiers', Sailors', Marines', Coast Guard and Airmen's Club
candidates.text:
Soldiers', Sailors', Marines', Coast Guard and Airmen's Club
A service member friendly hotel. The hotel is closed to non-military personnel unless accompanied by a service member, veteran, or military retiree.
Area: Midtown East; Address: 283 Lexington Ave; Price: Rates are based on rank; $25+

candidates.name: Soho Grand Hotel
candidates.text:
Soho Grand Hotel
The Soho Grand Hotel is a pet-friendly boutique hotel, featuring 353 guest rooms, ten suites, and two sprawling penthouses.
Area: SoHo; Address: 310 West Broadway; Price: $250-550

candidates.name: Casablanca Hotel
candidates.text:
Casablanca Hotel
Boutique hotel just off Times Square. High-speed Wi-fi and complimentary refreshments in Rick's Cafe 24 hours a day including breakfast in the mornings and wine and cheese receptions in the evenings except for Sunday nights.
Area: Theater District; Address: 147 W 43rd St; Price: $183+

candidates.name: Cosmopolitan Hotel Tribeca
candidates.text:
Cosmopolitan Hotel Tribeca
Clean, comfortable rooms with private bath and color television, plus wireless internet at a reasonable price.
Area: TriBeCa; Address: 95 West Broadway; Price: $200

candidates.name: Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan/Upper East Side
candidates.text:
Courtyard by Marriott New York Manhattan/Upper East Side
Free high-speed Internet & large work desk in each room, along with an exercise room open 24/7 with a wide range of equipment and services for everyone. A steam room is also present. The hotel is in walking distance of many close-by vibrant destinations along with quaint spots for any tourist.
Area: Upper East Side; Address: 410 East 92nd Street; Price: Member rate $117 per night; regular rate $119 per night

candidates.name: Hostelling International New York
candidates.text:
Hostelling International New York
HI-New York is the largest hostel in North America. Close to the subway, with internet, 24-hour reception, laundry, a lounge area, a small cafe, and no curfew. The building is old, but in decent shape and pretty clean.
Area: Upper West Side; Address: 891 Amsterdam Ave; Price: Dorms $45/night in the summer

candidates.name: Akwaaba Mansion
candidates.text:
Akwaaba Mansion
Four guest rooms, each uniquely decorated with a cultural theme, private baths (some with Jacuzzis), air conditioning and clock radio/CD player, wireless internet and business center, guest library, TV and game room, personal concierge to arrange tours, restaurant reservations, etc.
Area: Bedford-Stuyvesant and Flatbush; Address: 347 MacDonough St; Price: $160-175

candidates.name: Sleep Inn Coney Island
candidates.text:
Sleep Inn Coney Island
Free full breakfast, free WiFi, free daily newspaper, free coffee and free parking (first come, first serve basis).
Area: Coney Island and Brighton Beach; Address: 2586 Stillwell Ave

candidates.name: New York Marriott at the Brooklyn Bridge
candidates.text:
New York Marriott at the Brooklyn Bridge
The hotel’s luxurious accommodations boast a relaxed but modern atmosphere with state-of-the-art amenities.
Area: Downtown; Address: 333 Adams St; Price: 215-467

candidates.name: Holiday Inn Express Brooklyn
candidates.text:
Holiday Inn Express Brooklyn
Opened in 2006, the hotel features complimentary breakfast, wifi access and comfortable furnishings.
Area: Gowanus and Red Hook; Address: 625 Union St

candidates.name: Best Western Gregory Hotel
candidates.text:
Best Western Gregory Hotel
Free high speed internet access. Free continental breakfast. Lobby bar serves drinks 5-10PM daily. Meeting & conference facilities and business services.
Area: Southwest Brooklyn; Address: 8315 4th Ave; Price: $119–238

candidates.name: Greenpoint YMCA
candidates.text:
Greenpoint YMCA
Economy and deluxe rooms daily, weekly and monthly rates; higher prices during peak period. $99 for a double room.
Area: Williamsburg; Address: 99 Meserole Ave; Price: $48-69

candidates.name: New York LaGuardia Airport Marriott Hotel
candidates.text:
New York LaGuardia Airport Marriott Hotel
Offers a fitness center, swimming pool, flexible meeting space and complimentary hotel shuttle to and from LaGuardia Airport.
Area: Jackson Heights; Address: 102-05 Ditmars Blvd; Price: 159-319

candidates.name: Ravel Hotel, Trademark Collection by Wyndham
candidates.text:
Ravel Hotel, Trademark Collection by Wyndham
A luxury boutique hotel offering 63 lodging accommodations overlooking Manhattan with 9-ft ceilings, private balcony, and spa-like bathrooms.
Area: Long Island City and Astoria; Address: 8-08 Queens Plaza S

candidates.name: Dream Downtown - Chelsea
candidates.text:
Dream Downtown - Chelsea
With a tree-shaded lobby, metallic lizard banquettes, a glass-bottomed pool, and nightly DJs it is no wonder this place is so pricey. This ‘dream-like’ building has classic furnishing elements such as Turkish rugs and white Beverly sofas complemented with futuristic touches like shiny steel baths. Dream Downtown has created a beach club vibe with suites that lead onto the pool area, sandy patches, and outdoor cabanas. The hotel’s Ph-D Rooftop Lounge will serve up your favorite cocktails underneath their Venini glass chandeliers.
Area: Chelsea; Address: 355 West 16th St.; Price: From about $295 per night, depending on season

candidates.name: Comfort Inn Lower East Side
candidates.text:
Comfort Inn Lower East Side
If New York hotel prices have made you resort to sleeping under a bridge, this may as well be your choice (pardon the pun), as it consistently ranks as one of the lowest-priced decent hotels in the city, and is also almost literally located under the Manhattan Bridge. The location is a bit remote and not quite charming, but the hotel does not lack anything in its limited-service standards, although it is on the small side with only 43 rooms and most facilities sized to match.
Area: Chinatown; Address: 154 Madison Street; Price: $149, breakfast included

candidates.name: Conrad New York
candidates.text:
Conrad New York
Brand new all-suite luxury hotel overlooking the Hudson River in Battery Park City, located next to the World Financial Center and minutes from Wall St, Statue of Liberty and 9/11 Memorial.
Area: Financial District; Address: 102 North End Ave

candidates.name: Hotel Giraffe
candidates.text:
Hotel Giraffe
Free high speed Wi-fi and complimentary refreshments in the Grande Lobby 24 hours a day including breakfast in the mornings and wine and cheese receptions in the evenings except for Sunday nights.
Area: Gramercy Flatiron; Address: 365 Park Avenue South

candidates.name: Hotel Indigo Lower East Side
candidates.text:
Hotel Indigo Lower East Side
The idea of Intercontinental's Indigo chain is to provide a boutique hotel experience in a chain hotel, but many of the Indigos fail to live up to that. The one in Lower East Side, however, wholly does with a truly unique experience provided by its loft-like spaces and light, airy rooms echoing Scandinvaian designs, wooden flooring and practical designer furniture included. The supertall outlier in a low-rise neighbourhood provides multiple terraces as its slender build tapers off towards the top, one even includes a small pool. The Mr. Purple rooftop bar is an institution, and works of art can be found throughout the hotel. The only letdown may be the rather large room count, approaching 300 - meaning also that only the best rooms get the hotel's signature views.
Area: Lower East Side; Address: 171 Ludlow Street

candidates.name: Roosevelt Hotel
candidates.text:
Roosevelt Hotel
A Pakistani-owned hotel named after the 20th President Theodore Roosevelt and opened in 1924. The hotel has 1,015 rooms including 52 suites. This hotel has been seen in several major motion pictures.
Area: Midtown East; Address: 45 E 45th St

candidates.name: Salisbury Hotel
candidates.text:
Salisbury Hotel
King and double-bed rooms. Standard rooms are much larger than typical as the hotel was designed as a suite hotel.
Area: Theater District; Address: 123 W 57th St; Price: $109+

candidates.name: Hilton Garden Inn New York/Tribeca
candidates.text:
Hilton Garden Inn New York/Tribeca
The Garden Inn has a slightly dated chain hotel feel, but a reasonably nice restaurant and a strategic location. Rooms feature the usual conveniences found in midscale hotels, enhanced with a microwave and fridge that could be convenient for self-caterers, who will also find a hotel "pantry" with convenience food items for sale in the lobby.
Area: TriBeCa; Address: 39 Avenue of the America

candidates.name: Hotel Wales
candidates.text:
Hotel Wales
European style boutique hotel with numerous accommodations, free WiFi, paid parking, and elegant rooms with careful designs even for the cheapest traveler. Hotel Wales also prides itself on being an LGBTQ+ friendly hotel and has historically contributed to the movement.
Area: Upper East Side; Address: 1295 Madison Avenue; Price: 1 adult: Classic Rooms: $230 to $250; Junior Suite: $270; Suite: $270 to $300

candidates.name: Alfama Patio Apartments
candidates.text:
Alfama Patio Apartments
Two-star out-of-the-way lodging (but it's directly on the Tram line 28). Full amenities from fast Wi-Fi to free crepe breakfast only compliment the fun staff, who sometimes even go out with you at night.
Area: Alfama; Address: Escolas Gerais 3, Patio dos Quintalinhos 1; Price: 59-111

candidates.name: Lisbon Old Town Hostel
candidates.text:
Lisbon Old Town Hostel
A hostel, opened in 2007, catering to the young hip crowd with event listings on their website, free computer and internet access in the lobby and WiFi throughout the hostel.
Area: Bairro Alto; Address: Rua do Ataíde, 26A; Price: €15-22

candidates.name: Goodnight Backpackers Hostel
candidates.text:
Goodnight Backpackers Hostel
The interior design looks a bit like IKEA show-room, the staff know where the good places to go out dancing and drinking are and the location works for a budget traveler.
Area: Baixa; Address: Rua dos Correeiros 113, 2nd; Hours: 24 hr; Price: €18-20

candidates.name: Nau Palácio do Governador
candidates.text:
Nau Palácio do Governador
Five-star, 60 room hotel with spa, gym, two swimming pools, business centre, free breakfast, and free Wi-Fi.
Area: Belém; Address: Rua Bartolomeu Dias 117; Price: 119-248

candidates.name: America Diamonds Hotel
candidates.text:
America Diamonds Hotel
Three-star, 66-room hotel, totally reconstructed in 2006 in a historical building, keeping only its original façade, contrasting with its modern interior. Amenities include bar, restaurant, room service, free breakfast, and free Wi-Fi.
Area: North; Address: Rua Tomás Ribeiro 47; Price: From 62

candidates.name: Myriad
candidates.text:
Myriad
Five-star, 186-room hotel at the Vasco da Gama Tower offering panoramic river views. Amenities include indoor pool, spa, gym, restaurant, and bar.
Area: Parque das Nações; Address: Cais das Naus, Lote 2.21.01; Price: 187-272

candidates.name: Ibis Lisboa Centro Saldanha Hotel
candidates.text:
Ibis Lisboa Centro Saldanha Hotel
Two-star, 116-room hotel. Travelers give this Ibis so-so reviews noting on the plus side the location only 5 min walk to the metro, and a good breakfast and on the minus side small rooms.
Area: Alfama; Address: Avenida Casal Ribeiro 23; Price: 58-84

candidates.name: Poets Hostel
candidates.text:
Poets Hostel
The building is next the Chiado exit of the Baixa-Chiado metro station. Very helpful staff, clean rooms, dinners and activities are organized by the hostel. Big common room with TV and free internet. Dorms and privates available.
Area: Bairro Alto; Address: Rua Nova da Trindade, 2 - 5º; Hours: 24hr

candidates.name: Rossio Hostel
candidates.text:
Rossio Hostel
Great location, great staff, great free cooked breakfast, great hostel. The hostel offers dorms and privates. Free internet, TV room, lounge.
Area: Baixa; Address: Calçada do Carmo, 6

candidates.name: Vila Galé Ópera
candidates.text:
Vila Galé Ópera
Four-star, 259-room hotel next to the Tagus River. Adjoins Lisbon’s Congress Centre and the lively nightlife of Lisbon’s Docas area.
Area: Belém; Address: Travessa Conde da Ponte; Price: 64-173

candidates.name: Four Seasons Hotel Ritz Lisbon
candidates.text:
Four Seasons Hotel Ritz Lisbon
Five-star, 282-room hotel with spa, gym, swimming pool, restaurant, and bar. The decor is a mix of Art Deco and Louis XVI, with a collection of mid-20th-century Portuguese art.
Area: North; Address: Rua Rodrigo da Fonseca 88; Price: 465-777

candidates.name: Lisbon Story Guesthouse
candidates.text:
Lisbon Story Guesthouse
Cozy three-star, 11-room guesthouse with welcoming common areas and well-decorated small rooms at a budget price.
Area: Alfama; Address: Largo São Domingos 18; Price: 49-84

candidates.name: Oasis Backpackers' Mansion
candidates.text:
Oasis Backpackers' Mansion
Backpackers rave about this hotel, often noting the friendly staff, large clean rooms, fun atmosphere and great dinners. It is a great place for a budget traveler to meet up with other travelers and feel safe when they go to bed at night - if they go to bed.
Area: Bairro Alto; Address: Rua de Santa Catarina 24; Hours: 24hr

candidates.name: Travellers House
candidates.text:
Travellers House
Nice hostel with lots of extras. Friendly staff and easy to meet people with their nightly activities. Free WiFi, breakfast, coffee and tea, maps and city advice, lots of guide books to look at and a book exchange for travelers who are tired of reading the same book over and over again.
Area: Baixa; Address: Rua Augusta, 89; Price: Beds starting at €15

candidates.name: Intercontinental Lisbon Hotel
candidates.text:
Intercontinental Lisbon Hotel
Five-star, 331-room hotel overlooking Parque Eduardo VII. Amenities include fitness centre, bar, business centre, conference facilities, and free Wi-Fi.
Area: North; Address: Rua Castilho 149; Price: 133-257

candidates.name: The One Palácio da Anunciada
candidates.text:
The One Palácio da Anunciada
Five-star, 83-room hotel in a 16th-century palace with contemporary guest rooms. The old noble rooms now serve as dining areas. Guests can enjoy 2500 of gardens, two swimming pools, spa, fitness centre, meeting rooms, business centre, and free Wi-Fi.
Area: Alfama; Address: Rua das Portas de Santo Antão 112-134; Price: 145-263

candidates.name: Lisboa Central Hostel
candidates.text:
Lisboa Central Hostel
A fun, fresh and friendly place to stay in the heart of city in Marques de Pombal and Avenida da Liberdade. This international hostel provides a good base for sight-seeing by day and partying by night. All of Lisbon’s major night spots are easily accessible on foot.
Area: Bairro Alto; Address: Rua Rodrigues Sampaio nº160; Price: Dorms starting at €16

candidates.name: Yes Hostel
candidates.text:
Yes Hostel
Relaxed and comfortable hostel with an excellent location. One of the largest hostels in Lisbon; opened in July 2009.
